key_insight: A frozen vision foundation model can outperform specialized frozen EEG foundation models when EEG signals are rendered as task-optimized images.
engineering_relevance: SeeEEG enables reuse of pretrained vision backbones for EEG analysis while training at most 1,113 display parameters per view, plus a task readout.
method: Render each EEG channel in a dedicated patch row as a fixed-gain waveform or frequency-scaled scalogram.
Optimize montage, filtering, and contrast through a frozen vision backbone using task loss.
Evaluate frozen encoders with identical readout heads.
evidence_signal: Across eight datasets and seven EEG foundation-model baselines, SeeEEG with DINOv3 ViT-B led balanced accuracy on every dataset; random initialization reduced scores by 15.2 points on average.
watch_item: The results establish frozen-encoder performance, not superiority over fully fine-tuned EEG models; display optimization still requires task supervision.
paper_title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
